tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List the websites this key can access, with visitors in the last 24 hours.

tools.name: list_segments
tools.description: Saved segments (named filter sets such as "Paid traffic" or "Mobile in Germany") that can be applied to any report with segment_id.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Headline metrics (visitors, sessions, pageviews, pages per session, bounce rate, average session duration) for a period, compared with the previous period of the same length, plus a time series.

tools.name: get_breakdown
tools.description: Top values of one dimension (pages, entry/exit pages, referrers, channels, UTM tags, countries, cities, browsers, OS, devices, languages, custom events, outbound links) with visitors and sessions.

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Per-page metrics: visitors, pageviews, entries, bounce rate and time on page.

tools.name: get_realtime
tools.description: Visitors online right now (last 5 minutes) and what they are viewing.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Recent sessions with entry/exit page, pages viewed, duration, source, location and device.

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Every pageview and event in one session, in order.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Custom events (sent with pagelens.track) and outbound clicks with counts and their properties.

tools.name: get_errors
tools.description: JavaScript errors grouped by message, with occurrences, affected sessions and pages.

tools.name: get_web_vitals
tools.description: Core Web Vitals from real visitors (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB) at p50/p75/p90, overall and per page.

tools.name: get_journeys
tools.description: Most common page-to-page paths visitors take.

tools.name: run_funnel
tools.description: Conversion funnel: how many sessions completed each step. Steps are pages (path, * wildcard allowed), custom event names, or a page scrolled at least `threshold` percent (type scroll). mode: ordered (default; other pages may come in between), strict (each step right after the previous one) or flexib

tools.name: list_goals
tools.description: Goals with conversions and conversion rate for the period, compared with the previous period.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a goal that counts sessions visiting a page, firing a custom event, or scrolling a page at least `threshold` percent (type scroll). Needs a write key and member access or higher.

tools.name: add_annotation
tools.description: Mark a date on the charts (a release, a campaign, an outage). Needs a write key and member access or higher.

tools.name: get_retention
tools.description: Cohort retention of identified users (pagelens.identify): share of each daily or weekly cohort that came back in later periods.

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: Users active in the period: identified users (with traits) and anonymous visitors, with sessions, pageviews and first source.

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Profile of one identified user (traits, first/last seen, totals) and their sessions.

tools.name: get_search_console
tools.description: Google Search Console data for the site (when connected): clicks, impressions, CTR and average position in Google Search, by query, page, country or device, plus a daily series. Data lags about 2 days.

tools.name: delete_user_data
tools.description: GDPR erasure: permanently delete all events, session replays and the profile of one user on a site. Needs a write key and admin access.

tools.name: get_bots_and_ai
tools.description: Bot and AI traffic: AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot…), AI assistants fetching pages, search engines, and human visits referred by AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude…).

tools.name: get_ai_visibility
tools.description: How the site shows up in AI assistants, per AI company (OpenAI/ChatGPT, Anthropic/Claude, Perplexity, Google/Gemini…) and per page: crawler reads, live fetches while answering a person, human visits sent back, purchases and revenue, robots.txt access, and plain-language findings.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_errors · Public sink: get_retention · Destructive: run_funnel, delete_user_data.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_errors · Public sink: get_retention · Destructive: run_funnel, delete_user_data

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
